The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Tree With Paper Leaves

Daisy woke up with a splendid idea and a stiff neck. The idea was to invite the whole garden to the crooked-roof birdhouse. The stiff neck came from sleeping on her invitation.

“Everybody Day!” she read. Chip cheered. Caty tried the words out softly. Bella looked past the fence. “Does everybody know where everybody day is?” she asked.

Daisy took her invitation to Snail. “I can see the roof from here,” Snail said. Then he slid behind a clod of earth. “Where did it go?”

Under the lilacs, Moth had a different question. “I like company,” she said. “Will there be somewhere to fold my wings?” Daisy looked at the blank back of her invitation.

Beetle tapped twice on a hollow stick. “I have a song,” he said. “May I bring it?” Suddenly Daisy’s grand invitation felt much too small. She sat on it again.

Back at the birdhouse, a bare fallen branch rested in an old flowerpot. Bella tucked a scrap of paper on a twig. It looked exactly like a leaf. Daisy’s stiff neck went up straight.

“Let’s grow the answers,” Daisy said. “Pictures of ways to find us. Pictures of places to fit. Pictures of things to share.” Chip cut paper leaves. Caty set out the crayons. Bella found a stub just her size.

Daisy tied on the first leaf. On it she had drawn a bare branch, just as it was that morning. “This is our Welcome Tree,” she said. From down by the gate came two little taps.

Read together

What would help a newcomer feel at home here?
